title: Access Signal Retention Mapping and SDLC Integration Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook defines how access signals (authentication events, authorization decisions, privilege changes, and administrative operations) are classified, retained, and surfaced as compliance evidence across Redwood Inference. It also describes how those signals should be generated and preserved by engineering teams as part of the Secure SDLC so that we can satisfy audits, respond to incidents, and make measured risk decisions.

Goals
- Ensure completeness and traceability of access-related evidence for audits and incident investigations.
- Minimize retained data by classifying events and applying the least-retention principle while meeting legal and contractual obligations.
- Embed evidence generation checkpoints into the SDLC so feature changes do not degrade auditability.
- Provide a repeatable approval and exception process for access-control changes and retention deviations.

Scope
- Event types: auth successes/failures, token issuance/refresh, consent changes, role assignments/removals, IAM policy changes, privileged sessions, role-boundary crossings (cross-account/VPC), access-granting API calls.
- Systems: Redwood Console (auth service), API Gateway, Serving Runtime control plane, Dedicated deployment control plane, Private deployment provisioning services, SIEM and log archival.
- Not in scope: application-level business records (payment records, customer data payloads) except when they contain access-related metadata.

Principles
1) Evidence-first development: Instrument new endpoints or role changes with structured audit events before feature rollout.
2) Minimal retention: Retain only the fields required for audit questions; drop or redact PII from access signals where possible.
3) Single source of truth for classification: The Security Evidence Catalog (SECAT) governs event classes and retention tiers.
4) Defense-in-depth: Logs must be written to immutable append-only storage and shipped to SIEM within the ingest SLA.

Retention classification table
(Headers: Event class | Example fields | Retention tier | Primary owner | Reason / audit use)

Event class | Example fields | Retention tier | Primary owner | Reason / audit use
--- | --- | ---: | --- | ---
Auth grant / token issuance | subject_id, client_id, grant_type, scope, timestamp, ip | Tier A (7 years) | identity-platform | Long-term proof of consent/entitlement for legal and enterprise audits
Auth failure (suspicious) | subject_id, ip, failure_reason, timestamp, geo | Tier A (7 years) + security-alert snapshot | security-ops | For threat hunting and legal incident investigation
Role assignment / revocation | actor, target_subject, role_id, justification, timestamp | Tier B (3 years) | iam-team | Evidence for segregation-of-duty audits and compliance attestations
Privileged session start/stop | session_id, actor, target_resource, commands_executed (hash), timestamp | Tier B (3 years) | platform-sre | Incident reconstruction for privileged activity
Admin API change | change_id, actor, diff (redacted), timestamp, request_id | Tier A (7 years) | infra-team | Configuration change evidence and SOX/enterprise controls
Cross-region data-access event | subject, resource, source_region, dest_region, timestamp | Tier C (1 year) | data-governance | Data residency compliance and breach scoping
System health / heartbeat (auth subsystems) | component, status, timestamp | Tier D (90 days) | infra-observability | Operational troubleshooting only

Notes on tiers
- Tier A (7 years): Required for enterprise customers, regulatory needs (e.g., financial/legal), or where data residency/legal hold may be requested.
- Tier B (3 years): Standard compliance evidence for product controls and internal attestations.
- Tier C (1 year): Privacy-sensitive cross-border signals.
- Tier D (90 days): Short-term operational telemetry.

SDLC Integration checklist (mandatory for all code affecting auth, RBAC, or evidence generation)
1. Design stage: Add an Evidence Requirements section in the PRD describing which events must be emitted, the fields, and the retention tier.
2. Implementation: Use the org-standard audit logger library (auditlogger@redwood v2) to emit structured events. Schema must reference SECAT event_class.
3. Pre-merge CI checks: run `audit-schema-check` that validates the event schema, required fields, and whether any PII is present. Failing the check blocks merge.
4. Staging verification: End-to-end test that events appear in staging SIEM within ingest SLA (<= 120s) and match retention-tagging metadata.
5. Release: Release notes must explicitly list new event classes and owners for auditors.

CLI snippets and examples
- Validate schema locally: `./tools/audit-schema-check --dir ./src/events`
- Example structured audit event (JSON snippet):
{
  "event_class": "role.assignment",
  "actor": "svc:admin-console",
  "target_subject": "user:alice@customer.com",
  "role_id": "dedicated-admin",
  "justification": "onboarded by SE for pilot",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-09T18:22:13Z",
  "retention_tier": "TierB"
}
- Redaction example (preferred): omit full email and store `subject_hash` + minimal domain: `subject_hash: sha256(alice@customer.com)`, `subject_domain: customer.com`.

Ingest and archival SLAs
- Audit event delivery: 99.9% of events must reach SIEM within 120s of generation.
- Immutable archival: Write-to-archive acknowledgment must complete within 5 minutes of SIEM ingest for Tier A/B events.
- Integrity checks: Daily snapshot hashing and weekly cross-verify job between SIEM index and cold archive. Failures auto-create a P1 ticket to security-ops.

Exception and approval process (for retention or event suppression)
1. Submit an Exception Request in the Risk Portal with: scope, impacted event classes, justification, compensating controls, proposed shorter retention TTL.
2. Security reviews for risk scoring: security (primary), legal (for cross-border), product (for business rationale). Decision timeline: 10 business days.
3. If approved, owner must publish a compensating control matrix and implement SIEM alerting for anomalous access in place of longer retention.
4. All exceptions are recorded in the Exception Register (owner: GRC) and assigned a re-review date not to exceed 12 months.

Incident response: evidence preservation runbook (short form)
1. Triage: On incident that involves access or privilege misuse, incident commander triggers Evidence Hold flag in SECAT and notifies GRC.
2. Immediate actions (first 30 minutes): capture SIEM snapshot, lock retention policy for relevant event classes (override automated TTL deletions), and export signed archives to secure legal-hold storage.
3. Forensic capture: request `forensic-export` job for live system data (include request_id), preserve request metadata, and log the action.
4. Chain of custody: record actors collecting evidence, times, and destinations. Use `evidence-custody` template (see Appendix A) to track.
5. Post-incident: validate integrity of archived artifacts with the daily snapshot hashing process and store signed attestations in the incident ticket.

Operational ownership and dashboards
- Owners listed in the retention table are accountable for: alerting (missing writes), infrastructure capacity for archival, and yearly attestations.
- Dashboards: "Audit Ingest Health" (SIEM ingest delay histogram), "Retention Compliance" (percent of TierA/B artifacts with confirmed archive), and "Schema Drift" (recent PRs that changed event schemas).

Testing and QA
- Quarterly tabletop: Security, SRE, legal, and product run a simulated evidence-hold incident to ensure retention overrides and custody steps work.
- SDLC gates: `audit-schema-check` must be included in the codeowner CI for repos tagged `auth/*` or `iam/*`.

Appendix A — Evidence custody template (fill in for every export)
- Incident ID: 
- Export ID: 
- Requested by: 
- Date/Time exported: 
- Source system(s): 
- Files / artifacts exported (hashes): 
- Destination (location): 
- Chain-of-custody log (actor, timestamp, action): 
- Signed-off by (security/GRC): 

Appendix B — Minimal event schema (fields required for Tier A/B)
- event_id (uuid)
- event_class (SECAT name)
- actor (service or user id, hashed if PII)
- target (resource id)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id (correlation id)
- retention_tier
- signature (SHA256 of event payload, base64)

Related artifacts and next steps
- Create a one-time migration plan to backfill retention tags for events generated before this playbook. Owner: identity-platform.
- Add `audit-schema-check` to all auth and iam repo CODEOWNERS entries in the next sprint.
- Security to publish a short training session for product engineers on evidence-first PRDs.

This playbook will be reviewed annually or after any major change to the identity platform. Change history: 2026-02-10 initial published; 2026-03-01: clarified ingest SLA and added cross-region classification.
